clue.text: A laird's poet's rewritten poem

indicators.note: something rewritten is put down again in a new form, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish landowner's favourite bard has had a poem reworked.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the apostrophe-S endings are letters of the fodder: A LAIRDS POETS rearranged gives the twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's epic about the Fall of Man is the best-known long poem in English.

clue.text: Country girl's study

parts.note: Peru is a South American country
Sal is a girl's name (short for Sally); the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A piece of research about a young woman from some nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or examination, the same thing as a study of something.

clue.text: Smallest of family, a male, very thin, allowed to undergo punishment

parts.note: the runt is the smallest animal in a litter
he is the pronoun for a male
gaunt means very thin and haggard
let means allowed

explanation.surface: The scrawny youngest son of a household is permitted to take his punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from a military penalty where the offender ran between lines of men striking him, hence enduring an ordeal.

clue.text: Find not unduly noisy party

indicators.note: not tells us the next word's synonym is to be left out of the find

parts.note: a find is a discovery, something found
unduly means excessively, very much so

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a party that is not too loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find' looks like a verb but is the noun: a find. 'not unduly' removes VERY from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a dance party with loud recorded music.

clue.text: One of the 9, conductor said

indicators.note: said signals that the word is to be taken as it is pronounced, not as spelt

parts.note: Sir Malcolm Sargent was a famous British orchestral conductor

explanation.surface: A conductor announces he is a member of some group of nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the 9' points to 9-across, RANKS: a sergeant holds one of the military ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned military rank, so it is one of the ranks named in the cross-reference.

clue.text: Pool would appear old hat after transposition

indicators.note: transposition swaps the order of the two pieces, so the clue's old hat comes out as hat followed by old

parts.note: a lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Something swaps places to become a swimming pool, as if an old hat could.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool.

clue.text: Hurry up! Ale keg has spilt

indicators.note: beer that is spilt lands everywhere in disorder, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone urges haste because a barrel of beer has tipped over.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial command means get moving quickly, an informal urging to hurry.

clue.text: Counterpart of drunken toper in some pub

indicators.note: someone drunken staggers about, so the following letters lurch into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A drinker's counterpart is a soak in some pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes TOPER, IN and SOME PUB together, fourteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's opposite number holds the matching post in another organisation, their counterpart.

clue.text: In a cricket match, time to declare

indicators.note: In tells us time goes inside the rest, here between the first letter and the match

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: During a cricket game, the moment comes for the batting side to declare.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a captain may declare an innings closed; the surface plays on that, but 'declare' here means state formally.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to declare or certify that something is true.

clue.text: Series of soldiers controlled Kansas

parts.note: ran a business means controlled it
KS is the US postal abbreviation for Kansas

explanation.surface: Rows of troops took charge of a Midwestern state.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranks are rows of soldiers standing side by side in formation.

clue.text: After signal to stop limousine, pretty regularly see VIP on this?

parts.note: a red light is the signal for traffic to stop
a limousine is a type of car

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of pretty, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Once a stretch limo halts, you often spot a celebrity on this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' joins the pieces in order; the definition is a cryptic description of the strip rolled out for celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: A long red carpet is laid out for important guests to walk on at premieres and state visits.

clue.text: Glass vessel

definitions.meaning: a tall glass, for sherry or beer
a sailing ship with fore-and-aft rigging on two or more masts

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a large drinking glass and a fore-and-aft rigged sailing ship.

clue.text: Appropriate to disenfranchise?

definitions.meaning: a verb: to set aside or allocate funds or time for a purpose
read as ..., to take away the vote

explanation.definitionFit: To devote is to allocate time or money to a purpose; read as de- plus vote it means removing the vote.

clue.text: Connective material soldier put back inside …

indicators.note: inside places the soldier within the word the ellipsis leads to

parts.note: the ellipsis carries on to the next clue's jeremiad, here taken as lament

indicators.note: put back means the soldier is turned round, read right to left

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is sewn back into some connecting tissue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 15-across, so 'inside …' borrows that clue's 'jeremiad'; this cryptic reading genuinely crosses the gap, which is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: A ligament is a band of tough connective tissue joining bones.

clue.text: Bury the hatchet bestowed on Thackeray

definitions.meaning: an idiom: to end a quarrel and become reconciled
the middle name given to the novelist William Thackeray

explanation.definitionFit: To end a feud is to make peace, and it was also the middle name of the novelist William Thackeray.

clue.text: … jeremiad I found outside

indicators.note: outside means the founding word goes around the letter I

parts.note: to plant can mean to found or establish, as a colony

explanation.surface: Someone discovers they are surrounded by a long complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeremiad is a long mournful complaint, and a plaint is a lament or complaint.

clue.text: Plead for new sort of table

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are made into something fresh, a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone begs for a fresh kind of table.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop-leaf table has hinged flaps that fold down when not in use.

clue.text: Pick unknown for game

parts.note: to pluck is to pick, as fruit or a flower
Y is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Choose an unidentified one to play a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, game means brave and willing, the same as plucky.

clue.text: Fish rising to see bird

parts.note: a parr is a young salmon

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word to is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A fish leaps up to look at a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The parrot is a brightly coloured tropical bird known for mimicking speech.

clue.text: Pair encountering dragon move forward

parts.note: a dragon is a fierce, formidable woman, as is an ogress

explanation.surface: Two people meet a dragon and advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encountering' joins the pieces. 'Dragon' looks like a fantasy beast, but here it is slang for a fearsome woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To progress is to move forward or advance.

clue.text: Louder! State your views firmly

definitions.meaning: a call to someone to raise their voice
to give your opinion boldly and openly

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both raise your voice and express your opinion boldly.

clue.text: Produce document again, in entirety, perhaps

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone has to redo a document completely, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To retype is to type a document again, producing a fresh copy.

clue.text: Hand fruit around the country

indicators.note: around means the fruit wraps itself about the country

parts.note: an apple is a fruit
Aus is the abbreviation for Australia

explanation.surface: Someone passes fruit round the whole nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' looks like a verb meaning give, but it is the noun: 'give them a big hand' means applaud.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand is a round of clapping, so 'a big hand' means warm applause.

clue.text: See detective losing his head — that's bad!

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or look

indicators.note: losing his head means the detective's first letter is dropped

parts.note: busy is British slang for a police detective

explanation.surface: Look, a policeman beheaded: how terrible!
explanation.definitionFit: Lousy is informal for very bad or poor in quality.

clue.text: Place to stretch out and start to unwind

parts.note: to lie is to stretch out flat

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the word unwind

explanation.surface: A spot to lie down and begin to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu means place, as in the phrase 'in lieu of', in place of.

clue.text: Back-to back shows, lacking a skilled worker

indicators.note: lacking means one letter A is dropped from the joined shows

parts.note: an opera is a staged musical show

indicators.note: back-to-back means the second show is placed against the first facing the other way, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Evita is a stage musical

explanation.surface: A skilled worker shuns a pair of consecutive performances.
explanation.walkthrough: OPERA plus ATIVE (EVITA backwards) gives OPERAATIVE; 'lacking a' removes one A.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a worker skilled in a particular trade, especially in a factory.

clue.text: Asian zebu wandering towards capital of Kyrgyzstan

indicators.note: wandering means the animal's letters stray into a different arrangement
capital of means the first letter of Kyrgyzstan

explanation.surface: A humped ox roams towards Bishkek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towards' is a link joining the anagram to the final K. 'Capital' suggests Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan's capital city, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An Uzbek is a native of Uzbekistan in Central Asia.

clue.text: Plant responsible for venerable American carriages

parts.note: Ven is the abbreviation for Venerable, an archdeacon's title
a fly is a light horse-drawn carriage for hire
a trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: Some vegetation is to blame for old American horse-drawn vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'responsible for' is a link. 'carriages' gives two pieces, each a kind of horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venus flytrap is a carnivorous plant that snaps shut on insects.
